title: Implement temporal event foundation with PulseDelay
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Foundation Roadmap item 26 as one bounded vertical slice: establish exact pending-event ownership and chronological temporal execution through the existing machine and transaction architecture, using `PulseDelay` as the single opening temporal primitive.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed contracts created for this item

- `mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml`
  - status: reviewed; accepted reusable contract baseline
  - role: governs the ordered semantic calendar, stable machine-local pending-event identity, strictly future scheduling, equal-deadline batches, chronological ready-machine advancement, schedule reporting, runtime budgets, atomicity, and reference-path verification.
- `mossignal.node.pulse_delay`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/pulse-delay.yaml`
  - status: reviewed; accepted reusable contract baseline
  - role: governs PulseDelay's fixed shape, positive delay, exact reproduction law, temporal causality barrier, authoring, compilation, initialization, pending groups, inspection, provenance, identity, and conformance.

### Reviewed contracts reused unchanged

- `mossignal.runtime.reaction_scoped_pulse_foundation`
  - role: established typed Pulse batches, checked multiplicity, exact-bound initialization and delta input, Pulsed output events, reaction isolation, and grouped causal support. Its reviewed pulse semantics are reused only where cited evidence remains unchanged; its changed pre-stability fingerprint source is not silently reused as temporal authority.
- `mossignal.runtime.stateful_reaction_foundation` and `mossignal.node.toggle`
  - role: established previous/proposed state isolation, machine-owned family storage, same-reaction visibility, and single atomic publication patterns that temporal event proposals extend without conflating stored state with pending work.
- `mossignal.graph.authored_network_definition`, `mossignal.authoring.typed_network_builder`, and `mossignal.graph.structural_validation`
  - role: established dynamic definitions, typed and explicit-key construction, malformed-definition retention, and shape validation.
- `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_dependency_graph`, `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_cycle_validation`, `mossignal.compile.compiled_network`, and `mossignal.runtime.restricted_full_topological_evaluator`
  - role: established stable-subject dependency, acyclicity, immutable descriptor, private dense layout, deterministic settlement, and invariant patterns extended by the temporal barrier and due-event roots.
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle`, `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction`, `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction`, and `mossignal.runtime.policy`
  - role: established lifecycle, exact transaction binding, clone-and-swap staging, single publication, failure atomicity, result-owned provenance, and explicit semantic budgets.
- `mossignal.identity.time_domain` and `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint`
  - role: established caller-owned time-domain identity, semantic parameter sensitivity, insertion-order independence, golden vectors, and the synchronized pre-stability projection policy.

The existing ready-level transaction contract explicitly leaves temporal-deadline advancement uncovered; the new temporal execution contract owns that facet rather than broadening the settled level-only record. Snapshot/restoration, topology migration, and generic inspection facets recorded as `known_uncovered` are outside this bead.

## Included scope

- Add public `PendingEventKey` as a machine-local monotonic u64 serial distinct from private calendar storage, plus the smallest focused pending-event observation needed to prove stable identity.
- Add an exact ordered semantic event calendar mapping `Time<D>` to complete equal-deadline batches, with deterministic machine-owned records and no node-owned opaque queue.
- Add public `Schedule<D>`, ready-machine `schedule()` and `next_deadline()`, result schedule reporting, and structured pre-initialization rejection.
- Extend ready-machine application to process every deadline strictly before the requested time chronologically, combine obligations due exactly at the requested time with that current-time batch, and publish one atomic result containing chronological output events at their actual times.
- Apply existing runtime-policy limits to internal reactions, pending events, newly created events, evaluated operations, and required provenance growth without partial progress.
- Add `PulseDelayConfig<D>` with `NonZeroSpan<D>`, dynamic `NodeKind::PulseDelay`, typed convenience, explicit keyed construction, and exact stable fixed-port construction.
- Extend structural validation, temporal causality extraction, cycle validation, compilation descriptors, invariant checks, and full reaction settlement for PulseDelay's future scheduling and due-event emission paths.
- Initialize PulseDelay with no pending work, then process initialization and ready pulse input through the same exact delay law.
- Retain pending-group identity, owner, origin, deadline, count, revision, and result-resolvable causal contributors; remove fired groups and update the next schedule.
- Add focused owned PulseDelay inspection covering its definition before initialization and its pending groups, observed revision/time, and next deadline when ready.
- Extend the pre-stability version-1 network fingerprint projection with exact PulseDelay kind, port roles, delay, and temporal schema; synchronize authoritative projection text, affected contracts, and golden vectors in the accepted implementation change.
- Add permanent temporal-foundation, ordered-calendar, and PulseDelay conformance verification, including direct-jump versus chronological stepwise equivalence.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No TransportDelay, InertialDelay, Periodic, edge detector, latch, sample-hold, counter, temporal standard module, timeout, watchdog, or one-shot.
- No topology patch, duration-change migration, cancellation policy beyond semantic removal when a PulseDelay group fires, or reconfiguration-time handling of due events.
- No snapshot encoding, restoration, replay, execution/observable-state digest implementation, persistence decoder, or retained canceled-event history.
- No generic `inspect_pending` framework, compiled inspection plans, subscriptions, observer delivery, or complete explanation/why-not renderer; the focused PulseDelay inspection is the bounded opening hook.
- No forecast implementation, optimized heap/timing wheel/calendar, incremental dirty propagation, sparse transaction overlay, or performance-oriented event arena.
- No same-time scheduled events, timer threads, wall-clock reads, sleeping, automatic time advancement, or hidden global schedulers.
- Do not treat a PulseDelay's current input as affecting its current output, coalesce work across distinct logical deadlines, or give an equal-deadline batch semantic order.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement every requirement within the represented scope of the two item-26 reviewed contracts; keep their `known_uncovered` facets outside this bead.
- Reuse and extend the existing authored graph, report model, dependency/cycle path, compiler, full evaluator, machine store, transaction staging, runtime policy, output event, provenance, and fingerprint architectures; do not create a parallel temporal machine or transaction system.
- Represent pending work separately from reaction-scoped Pulse values and previous/proposed stored state.
- Allocate public pending-event keys deterministically and monotonically within each machine history, never derive them from private storage positions, and preserve the allocation cursor across every failed transaction.
- Enforce `deadline > current reaction time`; add `NonZeroSpan<D>` through checked arithmetic and reject `runtime.time_overflow` atomically.
- Process all deadlines before a requested target in least-deadline order and all events at one deadline as one unordered batch. A due PulseDelay group emits before removal; new same-time input schedules only later work.
- Preserve external input retention across internal deadline reactions and use empty reaction-scoped external Pulse input at those internal times.
- Publish each due external pulse at its actual deadline in deterministic chronological order, with every CauseRef resolvable through the outer transaction result.
- Ensure event creation, due emission/removal, schedule changes, PulseDelay inspection, time, outputs, and provenance are all part of the same candidate machine and single commit point.
- Preserve complete failure atomicity for deadline overflow, pulse aggregation overflow, and each applicable budget failure, including event records, serial cursor, logical time, state, outputs, and provenance.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Use the ordered reference map as the initial production calendar and choose the simplest deterministic record/batch representation; test and record the concrete choice.
- Choose one deterministic stable-subject order for event-key allocation when one reaction creates several events; test insertion-order independence and record the choice without treating it as stabilized compatibility policy.
- Keep equal-deadline PulseDelay groups separate or aggregate them through checked arithmetic, provided public keys and grouped causal facts retain complete observable meaning; choose, test, and record the simplest deterministic form.
- Choose focused inspection type and accessor names consistent with existing Toggle inspection patterns.
- Choose and record the exact pre-stability PulseDelay kind, port-role, delay, and temporal-schema projection spelling; no historical reader or migration is required before fingerprint stabilization.
- Extend existing runtime failure evidence minimally where `runtime.time_overflow` and named budget exhaustion remain structured and contextual.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/authored.rs` and `crates/mossignal/src/builder.rs` for PulseDelay configuration, fixed ports, and typed/dynamic construction.
- `crates/mossignal/src/validation.rs` and dependency/cycle integration for exact shape and the temporal current-reaction barrier.
- `crates/mossignal/src/compile.rs` for PulseDelay descriptors, due-event roots, future proposals, evaluation, and invariant checks.
- `crates/mossignal/src/machine.rs` plus a focused temporal/calendar module if useful for event records, serial allocation, ordered batches, schedule access, and PulseDelay inspection.
- `crates/mossignal/src/transaction.rs` for chronological internal reactions, event proposal/fire handling, atomic publication, schedule/result integration, provenance, and structured rejections.
- `crates/mossignal/src/identity.rs` and the authoritative restricted fingerprint projection for exact PulseDelay identity and golden vectors.
- `crates/mossignal/src/key.rs`, `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs`, and public exports for PendingEventKey, Schedule, configuration, and inspection values.
- Focused unit, integration, property/differential, and conformance tests.
- The two reviewed item-26 contracts and `docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml` only as required by independent review or the accepted exact projection; implementation-discovered contract changes remain draft pending independent review.
- `.beads/` when implementation acceptance synchronizes the bead.

## Required verification

1. Build equivalent external Pulse → PulseDelay → external Pulse networks through typed, exact-keyed, and dynamic paths; compare validation, causality, compilation, fingerprint, initialization, ready execution, inspection, and outputs.
2. Verify fresh initialization has no pending work absent input; initial counts zero, one, two, and larger values create only exact future work and no instantaneous delayed output.
3. Cover arbitrary nonzero initial times and non-unit delays, multiple origins, multiple PulseDelay nodes, fan-out, equal and unequal deadlines, and target times before, exactly at, and after pending deadlines.
4. Verify direct advancement across several deadlines equals chronological stepwise advancement in final semantic state, schedules, public event facts, provenance, and output events at actual times.
5. Permute definition, connection, input, event-record, and equal-deadline representation order and verify invariant semantics plus deterministic reporting and public event-key allocation.
6. Verify due input at T emits regardless of new input at T, while that new input creates only work after T; distinguish the due-event root from the future-only current-input path in dependency and cycle tests.
7. Verify `schedule()` and `next_deadline()` are read-only, agree on the least deadline, transition correctly between Dormant and WakeAt, ignore fired work, and fail structurally before initialization.
8. Verify every pending group inspection exposes stable key, owner, origin, exact deadline, count, revision, cause, and next deadline; private storage or batch ordering never becomes public identity.
9. Exercise checked time overflow, pulse aggregation overflow if aggregation is chosen, and each applicable runtime-policy boundary one below, exactly at, and one above; compare the complete machine before and after every failure.
10. Verify chronological Pulsed output ordering, grouped origin/provenance resolution, no pulse persistence, and no independently visible internal commit during a direct jump.
11. Verify fingerprint insertion-order invariance, delay sensitivity, distinction from Merge and other node kinds, exact port/temporal schema, and synchronized hand-reviewed golden bytes and digests.
12. Retain the ordered calendar reference path and compare any alternative calendar logic against it; run focused tests, then `make check-dev` and `make check-final` at implementation acceptance.

## Blocking questions

None. Calendar representation, simultaneous key-allocation order, equal-deadline group storage, focused inspection spelling, and the exact pre-stability projection are bounded deterministic implementation choices, not conflicting requirements, missing fundamental semantics, or frozen compatibility blockers.

## Readiness

Contract and bead review accepted. This is a bounded implementation-ready roadmap-item-26 slice with no product or design blocker.
close_reason: Implemented temporal event foundation and PulseDelay with chronological atomic execution, inspection, provenance, policy enforcement, canonical identity, and conformance tests

title: Add typed ModuleBuilder foundation
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Continuation Roadmap item 34 as one bounded typed-authoring slice: add ModuleBuilder<D> for reusable user modules, reuse the accepted builder-scoped Signal<S> and primitive-construction pattern, lower into the existing UncheckedModule<D>, and finish only through ordinary module validation.

## Roadmap provenance

- Document: docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md
- Item: 34
- Title: Typed ModuleBuilder foundation

This provenance records task sequencing only. Authoritative specifications and the referenced specification contracts govern implementation semantics.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed contract for this item

- mossignal.authoring.typed_module_builder
  - docs/specs/contracts/typed-module-builder.yaml
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs ModuleBuilder ownership, scoped typed signals, typed Level/Pulse module interfaces, duplicate and foreign identity handling, built-in primitive constructor parity, canonical unchecked lowering, and ordinary validation completion.

### Reviewed contracts reused without modification

- mossignal.authoring.typed_network_builder
  - docs/specs/contracts/typed-network-builder.yaml
  - role: supplies the accepted owning typed-builder, Signal<S>, explicit stable-key, structured foreign-signal, and completion pattern being adapted.
- mossignal.module.unchecked_definition
  - docs/specs/contracts/unchecked-module-definition.yaml
  - role: supplies the canonical owned dynamic module interface and private primitive graph representation into which typed authoring lowers.
- mossignal.module.validated_user_definition
  - docs/specs/contracts/validated-user-module-definition.yaml
  - role: supplies the sole finish-time validation and immutable ModuleDef boundary.
- mossignal.node.variadic_all
  - docs/specs/contracts/variadic-all.yaml
  - role: governs All typed/dynamic authoring, stable variadic ports, and semantics.
- mossignal.node.level_combinational_expansion
  - docs/specs/contracts/level-combinational-expansion.yaml
  - role: governs Any, Parity, AtLeast, and Select typed/dynamic constructor families and stable ports.
- mossignal.runtime.reaction_scoped_pulse_foundation
  - docs/specs/contracts/reaction-scoped-pulse-foundation.yaml
  - role: governs typed Pulse authoring boundaries.
- mossignal.node.pulse_merge, mossignal.node.toggle, and mossignal.node.pulse_delay
  - docs/specs/contracts/pulse-merge.yaml
  - docs/specs/contracts/toggle.yaml
  - docs/specs/contracts/pulse-delay.yaml
  - role: govern the existing Merge, Toggle, and PulseDelay typed/dynamic constructor forms and semantic configurations.
- mossignal.diagnostics.artifact_reports
  - docs/specs/contracts/artifact-reports.yaml
  - role: supplies artifact omission and report behavior for finish.

The reviewed primitive contracts have changed citations only in fingerprint or broad verification facets that this bead does not use. Their typed-authoring rules cite unchanged sources and are reused without reopening.

## Included scope

- Add deliberate public ModuleBuilder<D> construction for a caller-authored User module, with owned builder state, one private builder scope, and deterministic caller-local stable-key allocation.
- Add typed Level and Pulse module-input conveniences returning ModuleInputKey<S> plus Signal<S>.
- Add typed Level and Pulse module-output conveniences accepting only same-kind local Signal<S> and returning ModuleOutputKey<S>.
- Add the smallest consistent explicit stable-key forms for module inputs and outputs; reject immediately determinable duplicate interface identities through structured authoring failure and never overwrite an earlier claim.
- Mirror every built-in primitive constructor currently implemented on NetworkBuilder: Constant, Not, All, Any, Parity, AtLeast, Select, Merge, Toggle, and PulseDelay.
- Mirror the corresponding explicit NodeKey and stable port-key forms already present on NetworkBuilder, preserving AddedNode results, semantic configurations, stable variadic-port identity, source multiplicity, and ordinary structured failure behavior.
- Reject signals from NetworkBuilder, another ModuleBuilder, or any other foreign builder scope with AuthoringFailure::ForeignSignal before mutating the receiver.
- Lower the complete typed interface, private nodes, ports, connections, mappings, metadata, and explicit User origin into the canonical UncheckedModule<D> representation.
- Provide consuming into_unchecked and finish boundaries; finish must return Report<ModuleDef<D>, D> with behavior observationally equivalent to ordinary validation of the lowered UncheckedModule<D>.
- Add typed-versus-dynamic equivalence verification for representative Level-only, Pulse-only, and mixed modules, including stable keys, interface incidence, primitive configurations, deterministic inspection, diagnostics, and ModuleFingerprint after successful finish.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No module instantiation in NetworkBuilder or ModuleBuilder, ModuleBindingSet, AddedModuleInstance, instance outputs, nested modules, hierarchy, or instance-qualified internal identities.
- No standard catalogue descriptors, ModuleOrigin::Standard, StandardModuleDeclaration, standard-module constructors, aliases, or concise standard conveniences.
- No primitives beyond the constructor family already public on NetworkBuilder at this baseline.
- No changes to primitive semantics, dynamic node definitions, module validation rules, reaction causality, diagnostic taxonomy, or ModuleFingerprint schema.
- No network compilation, module flattening, runtime execution, machine state, transactions, observation, explanation, persistence, restoration, replay, reconfiguration, or migration.
- No macro authoring language, branded lifetime API, callback nodes, compatibility shims, speculative generic builder framework, or placeholder future methods.
- No public ability to use a builder Signal<S> as a durable module binding, persistence, runtime, snapshot, or replay artifact.

The typed-module-builder contract records standard-module parity, not-yet-implemented built-in primitive parity, module instantiation, and signal annotations as known-uncovered future facets. None is required by this bead and none blocks it.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement every requirement in mossignal.authoring.typed_module_builder within its represented foundation scope.
- Preserve Signal<S> as an opaque Copy/Clone authoring handle carrying signal kind, one builder scope identity, and one stable source reference.
- Make Level/Pulse kind mismatches and reversed module-interface direction unrepresentable through the typed surface where practical; send remaining dynamic defects through the established validation report.
- Check builder ownership before any mutation for every operation consuming one or more signals, including fixed, variadic, stateful, temporal, and output constructors.
- Detect duplicate explicit ModuleInputKey, ModuleOutputKey, NodeKey, InPortKey, and OutPortKey identities deterministically without overwriting or silently merging prior authored state.
- Preserve the accepted NetworkBuilder constructor semantics for the mirrored primitive family, including distinct Constant identity, stable variadic input-port multiplicity, exact AtLeast threshold, Select branch roles, Toggle configuration, and PulseDelay configuration.
- Reuse or faithfully share the ordinary NodeDef<D>, NodeKind<D>, NodePorts, ConnectionDef, ModuleInterfaceMapping, DiagnosticMeta, key allocator, and AddedNode representation. Do not introduce a module-only primitive graph or evaluator.
- Ensure into_unchecked preserves all successfully authored claims and User origin in the established UncheckedModule<D> shape.
- Ensure finish is observationally equivalent to calling into_unchecked followed by ordinary validation, aside from consuming ownership once.
- Keep ModuleBuilder scoped signals distinct from NetworkBuilder scoped signals even if locally allocated stable source keys happen to match.
- Keep production code free of unwrap and expect. Any panic must state and enforce a proven private allocator invariant rather than respond to caller-controlled input.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Extract private shared builder storage and constructor helpers, compose existing helpers, or implement a focused ModuleBuilder path. Choose the smallest design that avoids public API churn and duplicate semantic models.
- Choose the exact explicit module-interface method names and return shape consistent with existing add_* conventions; test and record the concrete choice without treating it as frozen compatibility policy.
- Choose the private builder-scope identity allocator and local key-allocation namespaces, provided builder isolation and deterministic authored results hold.
- Decide whether ModuleBuilder lives in builder.rs or a focused sibling module and how shared private lowering helpers are arranged.
- Reuse public AddedNode<O> or a strictly necessary equivalent only if the existing result cannot represent the exact stable node identity and typed outputs; do not add speculative result abstractions.
- Add task-focused private test helpers for typed/dynamic equivalence rather than a broad new public comparison API.

## Expected change surface

- crates/mossignal/src/builder.rs or a focused typed-module-builder sibling for ModuleBuilder, scoped interface authoring, primitive constructors, duplicate checks, and lowering.
- crates/mossignal/src/authored.rs only for narrowly required UncheckedModule construction/access compatibility.
- crates/mossignal/src/module.rs only for direct reuse of existing validation completion where needed.
- crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs for deliberate public exports.
- Focused unit or integration tests for module builder construction, failure atomicity, lowering, validation, and typed/dynamic equivalence.
- docs/specs/contracts/typed-module-builder.yaml only if implementation discovers a specification-backed correction; any such change returns it to draft until independent review.
- docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md and .beads for task state only.

## Required verification

1. Construct empty, Level-only, Pulse-only, and mixed typed modules and compare their unchecked definitions with equivalent dynamic UncheckedModule<D> values.
2. Verify convenience allocation is deterministic within a fresh builder and creates distinct stable interface, node, and port identities without silent merging.
3. Verify explicit module input/output identities and every explicit primitive identity/port form are preserved exactly; each duplicate category returns structured failure without changing prior authored state.
4. Verify same-kind module inputs can fan out, variadic constructors preserve each stable input-port identity and duplicate-source incidence, and outputs map to the exact selected internal source.
5. For every signal-consuming method, supply a signal from another ModuleBuilder and from NetworkBuilder, assert AuthoringFailure::ForeignSignal, and verify the receiver remains unchanged.
6. Exercise Constant, Not, All, Any, Parity, AtLeast, Select, Merge, Toggle, and PulseDelay through convenience and explicit forms and compare nodes, ports, connections, mappings, configuration, metadata, and validation results with equivalent dynamic definitions.
7. Verify into_unchecked retains explicit User origin and all authored interface/internal claims and does not validate, compile, or execute them.
8. Verify finish and direct UncheckedModule validation agree on artifact presence, deterministic diagnostics, ModuleDef inspection, and ModuleFingerprint for equivalent definitions.
9. Add compile-time or signature-level checks sufficient to show Level/Pulse interface and constructor mismatches cannot be expressed through the typed API.
10. Verify no instantiation, standard catalogue, nested hierarchy, compilation, runtime, persistence, reconfiguration, macro, or new authoring-language surface is introduced.
11. Run focused Rust tests while iterating, then make check-dev. Final implementation acceptance additionally runs make check-final.

## Dependencies

- Roadmap item 33 / ms-tjg is closed and accepted.
- The canonical UncheckedModule<D>, ModuleDef<D>, ModuleFingerprint, complete current NetworkBuilder primitive family, stable key vocabulary, structured diagnostics, and module validation path exist in the accepted baseline.

## Blocking questions

None. Exact explicit module-interface naming, private helper sharing, builder identity allocation, and local allocation namespaces permit several conforming designs. Select the simplest deterministic choices, test them, and record the concrete result for review.

## Readiness

The task is bounded and has no product or design blocker. The governing contract is reviewed and this bead is ready for implementation.
notes:
Implementation close-out:
- Added public ModuleBuilder<D> with typed Level/Pulse module interfaces, explicit interface identities, scoped Signal<S> handling, and User-origin unchecked lowering.
- Reused a private NetworkBuilder authoring core for the accepted primitive family, converting private external-input surrogates into ordinary module interface mappings during lowering.
- Mirrored Constant, Not, All, Any, Parity, AtLeast, Select, Merge, Toggle, and PulseDelay convenience and exact-key forms.
- Chose independent deterministic module-interface allocation namespaces and explicit add_level_input/add_pulse_input/add_level_output/add_pulse_output forms; these remain implementation choices rather than frozen compatibility policy.
- Added focused equivalence, primitive-family, duplicate, cross-builder failure-atomicity, validation, fingerprint, and compile-fail kind-safety checks.

Verification:
- focused builder tests: passed
- cargo doc tests: passed
- make check-dev: passed
- make check-final: passed

title: Add TransportDelay primitive on the shared event calendar
description:
## Objective and baseline

Implement roadmap item 46, `TransportDelay`, in `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md`, following accepted `ms-n0r` (SampleHold). Preparation baseline: `3909e6850b0f113c2e93c420bb7004e11bf749f9` on main, initially clean, with no open beads or governing specification/contract changes. The roadmap supplies sequencing; the following contracts supply the semantic basis.

## Contract basis

New draft:

- `mossignal.node.transport_delay` — `docs/specs/contracts/transport-delay.yaml` — draft. Required facets: `fixed-shape-and-configuration`, `declared-temporal-initialization`, `settled-transition-queue-law`, `temporal-output-and-dependency-boundary`, `same-deadline-chronological-precedence`, `focused-temporal-state-and-causality`, `transport-semantic-identity`, and the non-migration portion of `transport-conformance`.

Reviewed contracts reused unchanged:

- `mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution` — `docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml`: one ordered calendar, unordered equal-deadline batches, stable machine-local event serials and complete pending facts, checked strictly future scheduling, chronological advancement, exact-target batching, schedules, complete atomic publication, all five runtime budgets, and reference-calendar verification.
- `mossignal.runtime.stateful_reaction_foundation` — `docs/specs/contracts/stateful-reaction-foundation.yaml`: previous/proposed state, explicit initialization, family-specific private slots, independent machine ownership, complete settlement, atomic successors, owned committed-state inspection, and stateful verification. TransportDelay's specific current-output barrier is supplied by its node contract.
- `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction` — `docs/specs/contracts/initialization-transaction.yaml` and `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction` — `docs/specs/contracts/ready-level-transaction.yaml`: exact-bound input/lifecycle boundaries, LevelEstablished versus LevelChanged publication, result-owned causes, and failure preservation. Their opening Constant/Not scope does not limit the node/temporal extensions represented here.
- `mossignal.module.aware_execution` — `docs/specs/contracts/module-aware-execution.yaml`: ordinary recursive lowering, independent qualified state/event owners, transparent settlement and budgets, retained hierarchy, qualified inspection/provenance, and explicit-versus-module conformance.
- `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint` — `docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml`: deterministic semantic identity, representation exclusions, validated ownership, and canonical bytes/digest verification. The new node contract owns TransportDelay-specific projection inclusions; old restricted kind lists do not define its new encoding. Apply AGENTS.md's current pre-release policy.
- `mossignal.identity.module_fingerprint` — `docs/specs/contracts/module-fingerprint.yaml`: complete user-module projection, semantic parameters/state/temporal schemas, metadata and placement exclusions, and configuration-sensitive deterministic identity.
- `mossignal.authoring.typed_network_builder` — `docs/specs/contracts/typed-network-builder.yaml` and `mossignal.authoring.typed_module_builder` — `docs/specs/contracts/typed-module-builder.yaml`: scoped signals, explicit-key rejection, canonical lowering, module constructor parity, and structured authoring failures.
- `mossignal.graph.authored_network_definition` — `docs/specs/contracts/authored-network-definition.yaml`: stable typed dynamic claims, preservation of malformed claims, and the validation boundary.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model` — `docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-problem-model.yaml`: existing structured authoring/validation/inspection/runtime failure categories, truthful stable subjects and operation evidence, catalogue and failure-inventory coherence.
- `mossignal.runtime.policy` — `docs/specs/contracts/runtime-policy.yaml`: existing limit accounting, structured atomic failures, and below/at/above verification for implemented budgets.
- `mossignal.node.pulse_delay` — `docs/specs/contracts/pulse-delay.yaml`: unchanged PulseDelay scheduling, due emission, multiplicity, public pending identity/inspection, and provenance laws constrain the shared-calendar generalization and mixed-node regression checks. Its old projection-extension wording adds no compatibility ceremony to this task.

All cited sources of these 13 reused contracts are unchanged. No reviewed contract is reopened. Generic pending-event queries, snapshots/replay/digests, topology migration, and full explanation rendering remain known-uncovered outside this bead.

## Included scope

1. Add `TransportDelayConfig<D>` with positive `delay` and explicit `initial`. Provide `transport_delay`, `add_transport_delay`, and an exact-port form on network and module builders, plus dynamic closed-node authoring. The fixed shape is one Level input and one Level output; configuration contains no separate initial input/output values. Extend central schema, structured malformed-claim validation, compilation, exports, and relevant closed-kind inventories.
2. Compile independent remembered-input/output state and temporal descriptors. Current output reads prior output and due transitions; it does not depend instantaneously on current input. After its input has fully settled, compare it against the reaction's previous remembered input, stage that settled input as successor, and schedule one new target exactly at origin plus delay only when different. A terminal scheduling/state-proposal pass may reuse the existing PulseDelay pattern; it must not introduce an input-to-current-output edge or skip upstream settlement.
3. Initialize both remembered input and output from the same declared initial level with no preexisting transport work. The first differing settled input schedules future work while output remains initial. Preserve every later settled transition, including a reversal before the first transition matures. Due work changes current output and is visible downstream immediately; new same-time input schedules only future work and cannot suppress maturation.
4. Generalize the existing machine-owned ordered reference calendar to hold PulseDelay groups and transport transitions under one chronological execution/publication path. Preserve stable event serials, exact deadlines, owner/kind/payload/origin/revision/cause facts, public next-deadline semantics, and aggregate budget accounting. Consume a complete due batch before selecting settled transport output by greatest originating time. No duplicated opaque node queues, parallel temporal transaction loop, calendar optimization, or cancellation facility.
5. Provide focused owned structural/current TransportDelay inspection for direct and qualified module nodes: configuration, declared versus committed remembered input/output, current input/output facts, revision/time, pending identities and targets with origins/deadlines/causal roots, and next deadline. Retained inspections and transaction results must keep their exposed causes resolvable after later transactions. Distinguish current justification, state establishment, latest output transition, due obligations, and newly scheduled work. Preserve all contributors in a same-deadline transport batch, including superseded targets; no fabricated intermediate or unchanged LevelChanged event.
6. Integrate the node into deterministic network/module fingerprints with its kind, typed roles, delay, initial value, state schema, and temporal schema. Extend the provisional encoding in place, adding representative exact canonical bytes and digest plus sensitivity/invariance checks. Generalize temporal failure evidence where necessary so a TransportDelay overflow is not mislabeled as a PulseDelay operation. Preserve catalogue classifications and update public failure inventories for added leaves without inventing successful diagnostics.
7. All transport state, newly allocated event identities, due removal, new obligations, inspection evidence, outputs, provenance, and earlier internal-deadline reactions remain inside the existing candidate transaction. Checked-time overflow, serial exhaustion, runtime rejection, or budget exhaustion preserves the complete published machine and prior owned results.

## Implementation freedom

Choose the simplest deterministic private state-family and event-record representation. A focused remembered-input/output family and a closed heterogeneous calendar payload are natural options; do not force this two-value temporal state into SampleHold's one-value schema or introduce arbitrary-state traits. Helper names, slot widths, exact-port argument grouping, and cause-map organization remain private choices.

Choose one deterministic stable-owner order for mixed-kind simultaneous event allocation; preserve identity within a machine history and test insertion-order invariance. There is no frozen cross-revision allocation sequence. Preserve separate queued transitions unless a proven conforming aggregation preserves every required identity and causal fact.

Choose and record the simplest causal refresh convention when a matured batch leaves the same output value. Its full due ancestry must remain explainable, while unchanged output emits no fabricated transition and its latest output-transition cause remains unchanged. Focused owned causal access is sufficient; no generic explanation engine, observer/history API, or mandatory general StateChange collection is required.

Same-owner equal-deadline transitions with distinct originating times are not produced by the current fixed-delay public authoring path. Nevertheless test and implement the specified batch-selection law using a narrow private valid-event fixture. Do not implement migration to manufacture those fixtures. Conflicting indistinguishable origins are a future migration-finalization obligation, not a new ordinary runtime failure mode or a blocker here.

No unresolved product question. Ordinary encoding/representation choices require implementation, tests, and a recorded decision, not a prior specification amendment or compatibility freeze. Any implementation-discovered draft contract requires independent review before acceptance; material scope changes return to planning.

## Required verification

1. Exhaust both initial levels against equal/differing first settled input at arbitrary nonzero initial times and non-unit delays. Independently establish Ready states and verify repeated input creates no event, remembered input advances on every reaction, queued targets mature once, multiple pending transitions survive, and short-lived reversals remain observable at distinct deadlines.
2. Compare bounded generated histories against a small explicit transport reference recurrence and ordered event map. Include upstream stateful/combinational settlement, chains of transport nodes, downstream edge detection, and valid feedback crossing the temporal barrier. Permute construction, connection, stimulus, and due-event representation order. Validate the absence of instantaneous input influence and rejection of true combinational/current-reaction cycles.
3. Exercise due-time input before, exactly at, and after a deadline, several crossed deadlines, deadlines exactly at the requested target, and subsequent work created at internal reactions. Compare direct jumps with chronological steps for complete state, pending keys/payloads/origins, schedules, actual-time output events, and normalized causal meaning. Include mixed PulseDelay/TransportDelay equal-deadline batches and events from several qualified owners.
4. Privately seed a valid same-owner equal-deadline transport batch with distinct origins and reversed event storage order. Greatest origin wins; every matured obligation remains causally accessible; no intermediate edge/output event appears, including a final target equal to the previous output. Conflicting equal-origin migration finalization, patches at due time, and duration changes are explicitly deferred with migration.
5. Cover typed/convenience/keyed/exact-port and equivalent dynamic network/module construction, foreign signals on each constructor surface, duplicate node/port identities, wrong kinds/roles/arity/direction, missing or multiple drivers, and deterministic structured validation. Check delay/initial/kind/role identity sensitivity, metadata and insertion-order exclusion, and representative canonical bytes/digest.
6. Verify multiple independent machines, direct and module nodes, repeated instances and nested modules with distinct remembered/output state and pending owners. Compare explicit/module-wrapped behavior after normalizing intentional structural identity. Inspect before initialization and after scheduling/maturation, pending key survival/removal, initial versus committed values, exact origins/targets/causes, current support versus latest transition, and retained owned inspection/results after later reactions.
7. Force checked deadline overflow during initialization and Ready advancement, including a later failure after an earlier internal deadline; test maximum valid deadline and no wrapping. Exercise event-serial exhaustion through a narrow private boundary fixture. Reject after staged transport work using an existing rejection path. Compare complete lifecycle/time/revision, inputs, settled values, every state family and causal root, active diagnostic episodes, calendar and serial cursor, output baselines, schedules, and provenance before/after failure.
8. Check all five existing budgets below/at/above where representable: internal reactions, evaluated operations, pending events, events created, and required provenance growth. Aggregate mixed event kinds under the same limits and verify complete outer-transaction atomicity; public failure evidence must identify the correct temporal operation and stable owner. Preserve existing PulseDelay multiplicity, due-time behavior, inspection, and grouped causes.
9. Classify inapplicable inventory facets: no TransportDelay-owned cancellation, recurring schedule, conflict diagnostic, or episode producer; persistence/replay/topology/migration are later integration. Run focused authoring, validation, schema, temporal, stateful, module, identity, diagnostic, and transaction tests, then `make check-dev`. Corrective acceptance requires `make check-final`, closed-bead synchronization, and `make acceptance-record-check`.

## Exclusions and change surface

Exclude InertialDelay, cancellation/replacement of pending transitions, Periodic/recurring events, resettable temporal wrappers, new signal domains, topology changes and duration/connectivity migration, snapshot/restore/replay/digest APIs, generic pending-event queries, general explanations/subscriptions/history, calendar optimization, compatibility shims, and unrelated cleanup.

Expected files: `crates/mossignal/src/{authored,builder,node_schema,lib,validation,compile,identity,machine,transaction,diagnostics}.rs`, focused TransportDelay tests and affected temporal/module/transaction/schema tests and goldens. Small internal extraction is allowed if it keeps one shared calendar and transaction path. At implementation completion close this bead, synchronize .beads, and mark roadmap 46 DONE; preserve accepted ms-n0r.

## Research disposition and readiness

Task-scoped discovery covered TransportDelay/transport-delay aliases, initial state, settled transitions and causality, exact-deadline precedence, inspection/causes, authoring, identity/state/event schemas, testing, and reconfiguration. The eight new node rules own TransportDelay-specific findings; existing contracts own generic lifecycle, temporal/calendar, state, module, authoring, identity, policy, and diagnostic facts. Snapshot state/event sections ground current semantic schemas without adding a persistence implementation. Migration discovery identified future duration/connectivity handling and equal-origin rejection; their implementation remains excluded. The current-dependency contract was considered but not used for its changed compilation-test citation; the new node signature plus unchanged stateful/temporal facets suffice.

Bounded, open, and unblocked for the implementation sequence, with the new draft contract and bead ready for independent contract review. Preparation does not approve the draft or implement code. No source conflict, missing fundamental semantic, frozen compatibility promise, or other product blocker was found.
acceptance_criteria: Implement roadmap 46 TransportDelay with explicit positive delay and one initial Level; complete settled-transition preservation through the existing shared calendar; current-output causality barrier and exact due-time behavior; owned direct/qualified temporal inspection and provenance; deterministic identity; reference-history, mixed-calendar, equal-deadline, budget, and complete rollback verification. make check-dev passes; corrective acceptance requires make check-final and synchronized closed-bead acceptance checks. New TransportDelay contract remains draft for independent review; no product blocker or migration implementation dependency.
notes: Contract-task preparation completed at 3909e6850b0f113c2e93c420bb7004e11bf749f9 from an initially clean main with no open work. Added one draft coherent TransportDelay contract containing eight rules and 16 exact resolvable source heading paths; no reviewed hashes recorded. Reused 13 reviewed contracts, with all their cited sources unchanged. No existing contract or governing specification was edited. Task-scoped discovery mapped transport initialization, settled input/output and queue semantics, exact deadlines, inspection/provenance, identity, authoring, and conformance to the new node contract; generic temporal, state, lifecycle, module, diagnostic, identity, and budget facts remain owned by existing records. Migration, equal-origin conflict finalization, snapshots/replay, cancellation, recurrence, and general query/history surfaces remain outside the bounded task. Same-deadline greatest-origin behavior is covered through a private valid-event test fixture without adding migration. No product blocker; representation and causal refresh choices remain deterministic implementation freedom. Created the open bead with its closed ms-n0r dependency and marked roadmap 46 IN PROGRESS. Validation passed: contract catalog, all 16 draft source paths resolve, every source is cited, all 14 bead contract ID/path references agree, dependency/readiness checks, no implementation edits, git diff --check, and make check-dev. Draft and bead are ready for independent contract review. Author used --no-auto-flush and made no commit; the planning reviewer owns synchronization and the accepted planning commit.
