title: Validate reusable user modules and semantic identity
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Continuation Roadmap item 33 as one bounded validation-and-identity slice: validate the existing UncheckedModule<D> representation into an immutable reusable user ModuleDef<D>, preserve encapsulation and deterministic inspection, and compute its canonical ModuleFingerprint without introducing authoring or instantiation.

## Roadmap provenance

- Document: docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md
- Item: 33
- Title: Module validation, encapsulation, and semantic identity

This provenance records task sequencing only. The authoritative specifications and reviewed contract baseline govern implementation semantics.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed contracts created for this item

- mossignal.module.validated_user_definition
  - docs/specs/contracts/validated-user-module-definition.yaml
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs one-way module validation, complete interface conformance, ordinary primitive internal validation, module-local current-reaction acyclicity, immutable User ModuleDef ownership, encapsulation, deterministic inspection, and blocking reports.
- mossignal.identity.module_fingerprint
  - docs/specs/contracts/module-fingerprint.yaml
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs the opaque domain-separated ModuleFingerprint, semantic inclusion and exclusion, insertion-order invariance, identity sensitivity, validated ownership.

### Reviewed contracts reused without modification

- mossignal.module.unchecked_definition
  - docs/specs/contracts/unchecked-module-definition.yaml
  - role: supplies the accepted owned unchecked interface and primitive-internal claims, User origin, module-local stable keys, metadata separation, and lossless malformed-claim boundary.
- mossignal.diagnostics.artifact_reports, mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model, and mossignal.diagnostics.collections
  - role: supply artifact omission for blocking findings, typed catalogue-backed problems, and deterministic report collection.
- mossignal.diagnostics.subject_references
  - role: supplies stable module-definition, module-input, module-output, and internal subject categories. Its cited concrete subject section has changed only by an unrelated TimeDomainId clarification; the module categories required here were rechecked and remain unchanged.
- mossignal.graph.current_reaction_dependency_graph and mossignal.graph.current_reaction_cycle_validation
  - role: supply the established graph/SCC concepts and deterministic algorithmic pattern. Their module exclusions remain intact; module-specific integration is represented only by the new validated-module contract.

The exact version-1 user-module fingerprint field schema and module-specific private diagnostic condition keys are not frozen by authority. They are bounded deterministic implementation choices, not blockers.

## Included scope

- Add public opaque ModuleFingerprint and immutable ModuleDef<D> for successfully validated reusable user modules.
- Add consuming validate and borrowing validate_ref transitions on UncheckedModule<D>, returning the existing Report<ModuleDef<D>, D> boundary.
- Validate public input/output declaration uniqueness, mapping declaration existence, endpoint existence and direction, signal-kind equality, output completeness and uniqueness, and ordinary internal-input driver policy across interface mappings and internal connections.
- Validate the complete existing primitive internal graph using the established node-shape, port, connection, semantic parameter, initial-state, dependency-signature, and stable-key rules.
- Derive module-local current-reaction dependencies with public inputs as roots and public outputs as observations; reject every cyclic SCC and self-loop before ModuleDef construction.
- Retain explicit User origin, metadata, public interfaces, mappings, nodes, and connections in an immutable artifact with deterministic read-only inspection.
- Enforce private-internal encapsulation at public authoring boundaries while keeping internal subjects visible to read-only definition inspection and structured diagnostics.
- Compute a domain-separated BLAKE3-256 ModuleFingerprint from a canonical stable-keyed user-module semantic projection.
- Reuse the existing diagnostic/report architecture and extend the minimum module subject/evidence/code surface required for structured deterministic findings.
- Add focused positive, negative, order-invariance, metadata-exclusion, identity-sensitivity, and golden-vector verification.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No ModuleBuilder<D>, builder-scoped module signals, typed module conveniences, or changes to NetworkBuilder<D>.
- No module instantiation, bindings, AddedModuleInstance, instance-qualified identity, nested modules, or hierarchy validation.
- No ModuleOrigin::Standard, StandardModuleDeclaration, catalogue descriptors, canonical standard expansion, or standard conveniences.
- No network compilation, module flattening, evaluation, Machine state, transactions, runtime inspection, or explanation.
- No persistence envelope, encoder/decoder API, restoration, replay, compatibility migration, topology patch, or reconfiguration.
- No non-blocking module quality-analysis campaign beyond findings already produced safely by the reused validation path.
- Do not expose mutable validated graph state, private dense identities, callback nodes, compatibility shims, or speculative future APIs.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement every requirement represented by mossignal.module.validated_user_definition and mossignal.identity.module_fingerprint within their stated scope as independently reviewed.
- Preserve all mossignal.module.unchecked_definition requirements: unchecked construction remains lossless and does not validate or repair claims.
- Treat one public module input as a typed source that may fan out to multiple private input ports or remain unused; do not misclassify repeated input-key mappings as duplicate interface declarations. Count those mappings together with internal connections when enforcing private input driver policy.
- Require every public output to have exactly one declared, existing, direction-valid, same-kind internal source; reject unknown, duplicate, missing, dangling, direction-invalid, and wrong-kind output mappings.
- Reuse the established primitive structural and reaction-signature machinery rather than creating a second graph validator or causality model.
- Prevent ModuleDef construction whenever any blocking structural, interface, parameter, dependency, or cycle diagnostic remains; caller-controlled malformed modules must never panic.
- Keep ModuleDef immutable and ensure private internals cannot become external connection handles merely through inspection.
- Use stable module-interface and internal identities in diagnostics and inspection, never metadata, caller order, dense positions, or private allocation identity.
- Include User origin, typed interface keys, output incidence, all supported internal primitive semantic structure, parameters, roles, state/temporal schemas, and stable identities in ModuleFingerprint.
- Exclude diagnostic metadata, authored insertion order, private representation, module-instance placement, network bindings, and containing-network identity from ModuleFingerprint.
- Keep production code free of unwrap and expect.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Reuse or extract the existing validation passes, reaction graph, SCC implementation, canonical writer, and primitive fingerprint projections, or add focused private module adapters; choose the smallest coherent design.
- Normalize validated collections or retain raw storage behind canonical iterators. Choose one deterministic inspection behavior, test insertion-order equivalence, and record it.
- Choose the smallest forward-extensible User-only ModuleOrigin<D> representation without fabricating standard declarations.
- Define the smallest deterministic private module-specific diagnostic discriminator and evidence merge projections consistent with the catalogue. Test them, but do not present them as frozen compatibility policy.
- Select and record the exact pre-stability version-1 user-module fingerprint record and variant spelling consistent with the reviewed fingerprint contract. Preserve its complete canonical bytes in golden tests; no historical reader or migration is required.
- Add narrow read-only iterator or definition-graph view types needed by ModuleDef without implementing the broader compiled graph-query surface.

## Expected change surface

- crates/mossignal/src/authored.rs for validation entry points or narrowly needed authored access.
- crates/mossignal/src/validation.rs or a focused module-validation sibling for ModuleDef, interface/internal validation, reaction dependency integration, SCC rejection, and immutable inspection.
- crates/mossignal/src/identity.rs for ModuleFingerprint and canonical user-module projection, preferably reusing the existing canonical writer and primitive projections.
- crates/mossignal/src/diagnostics.rs for the smallest module-definition/interface subject, evidence, and validation-code integration required by this slice.
- crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs for deliberate public exports.
- Focused unit/integration tests and versioned ModuleFingerprint golden bytes.
- The two reviewed item-33 contracts only if implementation discovers reusable specification-backed corrections; any such contract change returns that contract to draft pending independent review.
- docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md and .beads/ for task state only.

## Required verification

1. Validate representative empty and nonempty User modules with mixed Level and Pulse interfaces and every currently supported primitive kind; inspect exact origin, public interface, internal stable subjects, semantic configuration, metadata, reaction relation, and fingerprint.
2. For each interface rule, cover a valid positive case and focused negative cases for duplicate declarations, unknown mapping keys, missing output mapping, duplicate output mapping, dangling endpoint, invalid direction, wrong signal kind, conflicting drivers, and an unused public input that remains valid.
3. Reuse focused primitive validation cases to prove malformed internal keys, ports, connections, arity, parameters, initial state, and dependency signatures cannot enter ModuleDef and do not panic.
4. Verify module input fan-out remains valid and contributes root dependencies, while public outputs observe exactly their mapped internal sources.
5. Reject self-loops and multi-node current-reaction cycles, accept structural cycles broken by established state or strictly later time, and verify deterministic SCC reporting under claim/traversal permutations.
6. Verify blocking findings omit ModuleDef, independent safe findings accumulate deterministically, validate and validate_ref agree, and an unchecked module remains unchanged after borrowed validation.
7. Verify ModuleDef is immutable, User origin is explicit, interface and graph inspection are deterministic, and inspection does not expose an external-authoring path to private internals.
8. Verify equal semantic modules constructed in different claim orders share canonical bytes and ModuleFingerprint; metadata-only changes preserve them; changing each included interface, incidence, stable-key, kind, role, parameter, initial-state, state-schema, temporal-schema, or connection category changes the projection.
9. Retain complete version-1 canonical digest-input bytes and expected BLAKE3-256 ModuleFingerprint for representative minimal and nontrivial user modules, and verify domain/type separation from NetworkFingerprint and other digest identities.
10. Verify no builder, instantiation, standard catalogue, nested hierarchy, compilation, execution, persistence envelope, or reconfiguration API is introduced.
11. Run focused Rust tests while iterating, then make check-dev; final implementation acceptance additionally runs make check-final.

## Dependencies

- Roadmap item 32 / ms-bnh is closed and accepted.
- The stable module key vocabulary, unchecked module artifact, complete current primitive family, ordinary validation/reaction machinery, report model, and canonical network fingerprint infrastructure exist in the accepted baseline.

## Blocking questions

None. The missing exact private diagnostic projections and version-1 module payload record permit several reasonable conforming implementations. Select the simplest deterministic choices, test them, and record the concrete result for review.

## Readiness

The task is bounded and has no product or design blocker. Independent review has promoted both governing contracts and accepted this bounded bead for implementation.
close_reason: Implemented validated reusable user modules, deterministic inspection and diagnostics, module-local causality validation, and canonical ModuleFingerprint; final acceptance passed.

title: Implement ready-machine level transactions
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Foundation Roadmap item 20: extend the restricted runtime with owned ready-machine level transactions at strictly later caller times. Apply exact-bound InputDelta values over the prior authoritative external valuation, run the existing full Constant/Not evaluator, atomically replace settled Ready state, and publish only genuine external LevelChanged events. Stop before pulse, stateful, temporal, patch, persistence, or optimized execution work.

## Contract basis

- `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/ready-level-transaction.yaml`
  - status: reviewed and independently accepted for reuse
  - role: governs explicit advancement values, Ready preconditions, strict time, delta retention, full settlement, atomic state replacement, LevelChanged events and causes, budgets, rollback, and verification.
- `mossignal.runtime.level_input_delta`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/level-input-delta.yaml`
  - status: reviewed and used unchanged
  - required facets: `exact-current-schema-binding`, `explicit-level-observations`, `omission-means-retention`, `deterministic-unordered-batch`, and `requires-prior-authoritative-valuation`.
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/machine-lifecycle.yaml`
  - status: reviewed and used unchanged
  - required facets: `explicit-runtime-lifecycle`, `machine-local-revision-and-identity`, and `mutable-ownership-boundary`.
- `mossignal.runtime.restricted_full_topological_evaluator`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/restricted-full-topological-evaluator.yaml`
  - status: reviewed and used unchanged
  - required facets: `compiled-immutable-input`, `deterministic-complete-topological-settlement`, and `reference-path-verification`.
- `mossignal.runtime.policy`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/runtime-policy.yaml`
  - status: reviewed and used unchanged
  - required facets: `explicit-machine-association`, `atomic-budget-failure`, and `implemented-budget-boundaries`.
- `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/initialization-transaction.yaml`
  - status: reviewed and used unchanged as contextual established behavior
  - required facets: the existing initialization constructor, apply path, result-owned provenance, budget accounting, and failure behavior must remain unchanged while Transaction and Machine::apply gain Ready advancement.

Temporal deadlines, complete provenance and result surfaces, state digests, and patches remain known-uncovered or excluded by the reviewed ready-transaction contract and are not blockers for this restricted slice.

## Included scope

- Add `Transaction<D>::advance(Time<D>, NetworkRevision, InputDelta<D>)` while retaining the distinct initialization constructor.
- Make the opaque transaction representation and pre-execution inspection lifecycle-aware without panics or compatibility shims.
- Dispatch `Machine<D>::apply` by transaction kind while preserving accepted initialization behavior.
- Require Ready lifecycle, exact expected revision, exact NetworkKey, NetworkFingerprint, and InputSchemaFingerprint binding, and a requested time strictly later than the current machine time.
- Add structured ready-application failures for delta-before-initialization and non-increasing time while preserving existing stale revision, wrong-network, foreign-schema, stale-schema, and budget distinctions.
- Overlay explicit level observations onto a cloned authoritative external valuation and retain every omitted value exactly.
- Invoke the existing full topological evaluator once at the requested time for the restricted Constant/Not topology.
- Atomically install the complete candidate external levels, settled levels, output baselines, output causes, provenance roots, and Ready time while retaining topology revision and runtime policy.
- Add `OutputEvent::LevelChanged` and emit exactly one deterministic event per external level output whose settled value differs from its prior baseline; emit none for unchanged outputs.
- Retain an immutable result-owned provenance view resolving every returned changed-output cause.
- Enforce every already implemented applicable runtime-policy accounting boundary.

## Explicit exclusions and non-goals

- No pulse inputs or outputs, PulseCount, stateful nodes, successor state, temporal nodes, event calendar, pending deadlines, chronological internal reactions, or schedules.
- No topology patch, target-bound delta, reconfiguration, migration, output establishment or removal, or revision advancement.
- No binding projection, caller metadata, expected execution digest, forecast, observer delivery, replay, persistence, snapshots, or semantic digest implementation.
- No incremental dirty propagation, sparse staging, undo log, callback-based execution, or performance optimization.
- Do not expand the complete diagnostic Problem kernel or full RuntimeFailure layering beyond the exact reachable categories needed by this slice.
- Do not change InputSnapshot completeness or initialization LevelEstablished behavior.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement `owned-explicit-advance-value`, `exact-ready-preconditions`, `strictly-later-caller-time`, `delta-overlay-retention`, `ordinary-restricted-settlement`, `complete-ready-state-on-success`, `changed-output-events`, `resolvable-ready-causes`, `applicable-runtime-policy-budgets`, `single-atomic-publication`, `failure-preserves-complete-machine`, and `restricted-ready-verification` from `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction`.
- Use stable identities from the compiled machine and delta rather than dense positions or caller-supplied surrogate schema context.
- Preserve the first observation when rejecting invalid construction earlier; application consumes an already valid delta and must not reinterpret omission as Low.
- Compare every newly settled external level output against the prior committed baseline before replacement. Event order must be deterministic by stable semantic identity and must not encode causal order.
- Every returned CauseRef must resolve through the returned TransactionResult provenance after later transactions run.
- Keep every fallible step before one complete MachineStore replacement. Rejections must preserve a full semantic before/after observation, including prior provenance sharing and output causes.
- A successful state-only transaction advances Ready time but keeps before_revision equal to after_revision.
- Preserve generic behavior without adding unrelated bounds on D.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Private Transaction variant representation, lifecycle-aware input accessor spelling, helper extraction between initialization and advancement, and module placement are free. The current initialization-only `Transaction::input()` accessor is not an authoritative cross-variant promise; replace it with a non-panicking coherent inspection surface rather than retain it through panic or a compatibility shim.
- Clone-and-swap or an equivalently simple complete MachineStore candidate is preferred. Choose the simplest deterministic implementation, test it, and record the concrete choice.
- Provenance may reuse immutable prior records or construct a replacement view when result-owned causes remain resolvable and required current roots survive.
- Private event and provenance ordering/storage are free and are not public iteration or persistence promises.
- Budgets with no represented work in this slice need no invented accounting.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/transaction.rs` for transaction variants, ready application, failures, LevelChanged results, provenance, and focused tests.
- `crates/mossignal/src/input.rs` only for a minimal crate-private owned delta projection if needed.
- `crates/mossignal/src/machine.rs` only for candidate-state or current-cause support needed by ready application.
- `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs` only for deliberate public exports or adjusted transaction inspection types.
- `docs/specs/contracts/ready-level-transaction.yaml` only for implementation-discovered reusable specification-backed corrections; any implementation change remains draft and requires independent review.
- `.beads/` when implementation acceptance closes and synchronizes the bead.

## Required verification

1. Initialize, then apply empty, single-input, partial, complete, and explicit-reassertion deltas at strictly later arbitrary times.
2. Verify omitted Low and High external levels retain their exact prior values and explicit observations form one unordered batch.
3. Verify complete Constant/Not reevaluation and settled state replacement, including multi-layer and reconvergent restricted graphs.
4. Verify LevelChanged carries exact from, to, time, unchanged revision, stable output identity, and a result-resolvable acyclic cause; unchanged outputs emit no event.
5. Verify deterministic equivalent results under delta insertion order, authored insertion order, and diagnostic metadata changes without treating representation order as causality.
6. Verify successful state-only transactions advance time while retaining NetworkRevision and RuntimePolicyId.
7. Verify structured rejection for advance-before-initialization, equal time, earlier time, stale revision, wrong network, foreign schema, stale schema, and each applicable budget one below, exactly at, and one above its boundary where representable.
8. For every rejection, compare the complete machine observation before and after, including time, external levels, settled levels, baselines, causes, and provenance ownership.
9. Verify initialization transactions still produce the accepted Ready state and LevelEstablished events, and initialization applied to Ready remains rejected without mutation.
10. Run focused Rust tests while iterating, then `make check-dev`; final acceptance additionally runs `make check-final`.

## Dependencies and readiness

Roadmap item 19 (`ms-ipi`) is closed and accepted. The reviewed delta, lifecycle, evaluator, policy, and initialization contracts are unchanged. The ready-machine transaction contract is reviewed, internally consistent, and has no unresolved product question, conflicting requirement, missing fundamental semantic rule, or frozen compatibility blocker. This bead is bounded and ready for implementation.

description:

- No structural validation, diagnostic emission, `Report` production, private validation candidate, reaction dependencies, cycle checking, `ValidatedNetwork`, dense indices, compilation, machine/runtime execution, modules, persistence encoding, or topology patches.
- Do not add placeholder semantics for node kinds beyond `Constant` and `Not`.
- Do not make constructor-time validity checks that discard or rewrite malformed authored input.

## Implementation obligations

- Keep the representation authoritative and stable-keyed; no dense runtime positions or evaluator scheduling belong here.
- Model external endpoints as network boundaries rather than nodes.
- Constant definitions must record their `LogicLevel` configuration and level output shape; Not definitions must record their one level input and level output shape.
- Preserve signal kind in all typed endpoints; erasure is allowed only for heterogeneous storage and must retain the kind.
- Keep the public API owned and non-callback-based.
- Add concise `SPEC:` comments only where a non-obvious lossless-storage choice prevents weakening the malformed-input boundary.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Private collection layout is free provided it losslessly preserves duplicate and malformed claims.
- Exact constructor/helper naming and module-internal layout are free.
- The representation may use simple vectors as the canonical opening storage.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs`
- new authored-graph source module and its focused unit tests
- `docs/specs/contracts/authored-network-definition.yaml` only if implementation discovers additional specification-backed facts (any such change remains draft)

## Required verification

- Run `make check-dev` before completion and `make check-final` for final acceptance.
- Do not claim validation behavior; the next roadmap item owns validation-focused positive/negative conformance cases.

## Readiness

Accepted for implementation. No unresolved observable product question blocks this bounded slice.

title: Implement stateful reaction foundation with Toggle
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Foundation Roadmap item 25 as one bounded vertical slice: establish previous/proposed state ownership and atomic state commitment through the existing reaction and transaction architecture, using the Pulse-controlled `Toggle` as the single opening stateful primitive.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed contracts for this item

- `mossignal.runtime.stateful_reaction_foundation`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/stateful-reaction-foundation.yaml`
  - status: reviewed; accepted for reuse at the recorded evidence baseline
  - role: governs previous/proposed state isolation, declared-state initialization, state-family slots, same-reaction visibility, atomic commitment, direct inspection, and foundation verification.
- `mossignal.node.toggle`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/toggle.yaml`
  - status: reviewed; accepted for reuse at the recorded evidence baseline
  - role: governs Toggle's fixed shape, explicit initial state, parity law, authoring, causality, compilation, inspection, provenance, identity, and conformance.

### Reviewed contracts reused unchanged

- `mossignal.runtime.reaction_scoped_pulse_foundation` and `mossignal.node.pulse_merge`
  - role: established typed Pulse batches, exact-bound input artifacts, reaction-local multiplicity, grouped provenance, and the existing Pulse authoring/runtime path consumed by Toggle.
- `mossignal.graph.authored_network_definition`, `mossignal.authoring.typed_network_builder`, and `mossignal.graph.structural_validation`
  - role: established dynamic definitions, typed and explicit-key builder patterns, malformed-definition retention, and shape validation.
- `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_dependency_graph` and `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_cycle_validation`
  - role: established conservative dependency extraction and cycle rejection, including the rule that a whole stateful node is not automatically a causality barrier.
- `mossignal.compile.compiled_network` and `mossignal.runtime.restricted_full_topological_evaluator`
  - role: established immutable descriptors, private dense storage, deterministic full settlement, and compiled invariant checks. Changed evidence in this contract, the structural-validation contract, and the reaction dependency and cycle contracts was rechecked against current authority; it preserves the represented stable-subject, private-candidate, deterministic-cycle, and private-dense-layout rules without contradiction.
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle`, `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction`, and `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction`
  - role: established independent machine stores, ordinary initialization and ready reactions, clone-and-swap staging, single publication, failure atomicity, and result-owned provenance.
- `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint`
  - role: established semantic parameter and state-schema contribution, insertion-order independence, golden vectors, and the synchronized pre-stability projection policy.

The contracts' snapshot/restoration and topology-migration `known_uncovered` facets are intentionally outside this item. Authored Toggle cycle conformance also waits for a separately implemented Level-to-Pulse primitive; this slice verifies Toggle's immediate dependency signature without adding another primitive.

## Included scope

- Add public `ToggleConfig` with an explicit initial `LogicLevel` and add closed dynamic `NodeKind::Toggle` with exactly one Pulse input and one Level output.
- Add typed convenience, explicit keyed, and exact fixed-port Toggle construction through the existing `NetworkBuilder` and unchecked authored representation.
- Extend structural validation, current-reaction dependency extraction, cycle validation integration, compilation, and invariant checks for Toggle.
- Add exactly one Toggle-family state cell per valid Toggle, with declared state in AwaitingInitialization and independent mutable state per spawned machine.
- Extend the full topological evaluator so every operation reads previous committed Toggle state, computes the parity-law current output and one proposed successor, exposes that output downstream in the same reaction, and never overwrites committed state during evaluation.
- Integrate proposed-state staging and one atomic successor commit into both initialization and ready transactions, preserving complete failure atomicity and result-resolvable causal support.
- Add the smallest owned node-inspection surface needed to expose Toggle's declared initial state before initialization and its committed state, observed revision/time, and applicable latest inversion cause when ready.
- Extend the pre-stability version-1 network fingerprint projection with Toggle's exact kind, fixed port roles, state schema, and initial-level parameter; synchronize the authoritative projection, network-fingerprint contract, and golden vectors in the accepted implementation change.
- Add focused stateful-foundation and exhaustive Toggle conformance verification.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No RisingEdge, FallingEdge, AnyEdge, set/reset latch, SampleHold, counter, finite-state-machine, additional state family, or broader pulse-combinational primitive.
- No temporal node, pending event, schedule change, deadline execution, topology patch, state migration, persistence encoding or decoding, snapshot restoration, replay, or semantic state digest.
- No reset port or resettable Toggle primitive; resettable behavior remains a later standard module or separately specified node.
- No generic inspection-query compiler, subscriptions, observer deltas, retained pulse history system, or complete explanation/why-not renderer.
- No incremental dirty propagation, sparse state overlay, undo log, callback evaluator, trait-object node state, or performance optimization.
- Do not make proposed state publicly visible as committed state, feed it back within the same reaction, or treat Toggle as a blanket current-reaction causality barrier.
- Do not require `StateChange` publication in this opening slice; direct committed-state inspection is required, and later reporting may add the recommended change-set representation.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement the product and verification requirements within this bead's stated scope from the two reviewed item-25 contracts; their `known_uncovered` facets remain out of scope.
- Reuse the existing authored graph, report model, reaction dependency graph, compiler, full evaluator, machine lifecycle, transaction, input artifact, output-event, provenance, and fingerprint paths; do not create a parallel stateful execution architecture.
- Preserve the complete previous-state vector until all reaction operations have produced their settled outputs and proposals, then commit all successors exactly once with the rest of the candidate machine.
- Treat Toggle's complete simultaneous count by parity: zero and every even count retain the prior level; every odd count inverts it once, regardless of count magnitude or insertion order.
- Preserve current downstream visibility: Toggle's current Level output may drive later combinational or stateful operations in the same acyclic topological reaction.
- Use declared initial state as the first reaction's previous state and process initialization pulses through the ordinary law before publishing `LevelEstablished` and committing the first successor.
- Preserve latest inversion causality across even-count reactions; an even batch may support the current output explanation but must not fabricate a new inversion.
- Ensure every structured transaction rejection preserves Toggle state, settled signals, output baselines, logical time, provenance, and every existing complete-machine observation.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Choose the simplest deterministic Toggle state-family vectors, dense state-slot index, descriptor fields, proposal staging, and clone-and-swap decomposition; test and record the concrete choice.
- Fixed port keys may be derived deterministically or allocated consistently with the established builder, while exact-keyed dynamic construction remains durable reconstruction authority.
- Choose and record the exact canonical Toggle and state-schema variant spelling for the synchronized pre-stability projection; no historical reader or migration is required before fingerprint stabilization.
- The focused inspection value and accessor names are ordinary API design freedom if they are owned, revision/time-aware when ready, distinguish declared from committed state, and fail structurally for unavailable runtime facts.

## Expected change surface

- `crates/mossignal/src/authored.rs` and `crates/mossignal/src/builder.rs` for Toggle configuration, ports, and typed/dynamic authoring.
- `crates/mossignal/src/validation.rs` and dependency/cycle integration for shape and current-reaction causality.
- `crates/mossignal/src/compile.rs` for Toggle descriptors, state-slot layout, full evaluation, proposed successors, and invariant checks.
- `crates/mossignal/src/machine.rs` for declared/committed Toggle state ownership and focused node inspection.
- `crates/mossignal/src/transaction.rs` for state staging, atomic commitment, output/provenance integration, and rejection regression tests.
- `crates/mossignal/src/identity.rs` and the authoritative restricted fingerprint projection for exact Toggle identity and golden vectors.
- `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs` for deliberate public configuration and inspection exports.
- `docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml` only as required by the accepted exact pre-stability projection; the selected reviewed contracts remain unchanged unless implementation discovers a reusable specification-backed correction.
- `.beads/` when implementation acceptance synchronizes the bead.

## Required verification

1. Exhaust both previous levels with counts zero, one, two, three, a larger even count, and a larger odd count; verify current output and committed successor exactly follow parity.
2. Initialize Low and High Toggle definitions with absent, even, and odd pulse batches; verify declared state is the previous state, settled output is established, and the successor commits once.
3. Apply later absent/even/odd pulse transactions and verify strict reaction isolation, state retention or one inversion, exact LevelChanged suppression/publication, and latest inversion cause retention.
4. Build equivalent Toggle networks through typed, explicit-keyed, and direct dynamic paths; compare validation, dependency graph, compilation, fingerprints, initialization, later transactions, inspection, and observable outputs.
5. Verify Pulse→Toggle→Level-combinational downstream chains settle in the same reaction and verify dependency extraction records Toggle's instantaneous Pulse-to-Level edge without treating the whole stateful node as a causality barrier. Authored cycle conformance waits for a separately implemented Level-to-Pulse primitive.
6. Spawn multiple machines from one compiled network and verify their Toggle state evolves independently while the compiled topology remains immutable.
7. Verify pre-initialization inspection exposes definition and declared initial state but rejects unavailable current runtime facts; ready inspection exposes committed state, revision/time, and latest inversion cause without exposing proposed state.
8. Force each applicable existing structured rejection and compare the complete machine before and after, including Toggle state and state causes; no proposal or partial output may leak.
9. Verify same-topology insertion-order fingerprint invariance, sensitivity to initial level and Toggle versus other node kinds, exact fixed roles/state schema, and synchronized hand-reviewed golden bytes and digests.
10. Run focused Rust tests while iterating, then `make check-dev` and `make check-final` at implementation acceptance.

## Blocking questions

None. Private state layout, focused inspection spelling, and the exact pre-stability canonical Toggle variant are bounded deterministic implementation choices, not missing fundamental semantics or frozen compatibility blockers.

## Readiness

Confirmed as a bounded roadmap-item-25 implementation bead against the two reviewed contracts. No product or design blocker prevents progress.
close_reason: Implemented stateful reaction foundation with Toggle, synchronized fingerprint authority and reviewed contracts, and passed final acceptance.

title: Implement restricted semantic fingerprints and input-schema identity
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Foundation Roadmap item 12 for the restricted level-only Constant/Not model: make caller-owned time-domain identity intrinsic to authored networks, compute exact version-1 network and input-schema fingerprints after successful validation, and expose those identities before dense compilation and input artifacts.

## Contract basis

- `mossignal.graph.authored_network_definition`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/authored-network-definition.yaml`
  - status: reviewed, used unchanged
  - role: stable-keyed restricted authored structure and the exclusion of diagnostic metadata from semantics.

- `mossignal.graph.current_reaction_cycle_validation`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/current-reaction-cycle-validation.yaml`
  - status: reviewed, used unchanged
  - role: successful restricted validation and the opaque ValidatedNetwork lifecycle boundary.

- `mossignal.identity.time_domain`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/time-domain-identity.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: caller-owned identity, authored-stage binding, lifecycle retention, persistence verification, and fingerprint contribution.

- `mossignal.identity.network_fingerprint`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/network-fingerprint.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: public opaque value, exact restricted v1 projection, BLAKE3 domain separation, exclusions, ownership, and verification.

- `mossignal.identity.input_schema_fingerprint`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/input-schema-fingerprint.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: exact restricted v1 external-input-schema identity, separate network binding, ownership, and verification.

## Included scope

- Introduce public opaque `TimeDomainId`, `NetworkFingerprint`, and `InputSchemaFingerprint` values for the restricted model.
- Bind one caller-supplied `TimeDomainId` to `UncheckedNetwork<D>` construction and carry it unchanged through successful validation.
- Compute and expose both fingerprints on `ValidatedNetwork<D>`; preserve them for item 13 to carry unchanged into `CompiledNetwork<D>`.
- Implement only the narrow canonical CBOR value encoder needed for the two exact version-1 digest projections.
- Encode the frozen restricted network projection covering version 1 core and built-in semantics, network and time-domain identity, Constant/Not nodes, stable typed ports and roles, connections, external endpoints, and Constant values.
- Encode the frozen restricted input-schema projection covering canonically ordered external level inputs with required establishment semantics.
- Compute domain-separated unkeyed BLAKE3-256 values with the exact network and input-schema labels.
- Provide stable lowercase hexadecimal formatting and the specified ordinary value traits.
- Add golden-vector, semantic-sensitivity, domain-separation, exclusion, and permutation tests.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- Do not implement `CompiledNetwork`, dense indices, evaluator descriptors, machine state, `RuntimePolicy`, `InputSnapshot`, `InputDelta`, topology revisions, patches, snapshots, replay, state digests, or complete persistence artifacts.
- Do not implement artifact prefixes, envelopes, encoding APIs, decoding, schema upgrades, compatibility tables, or persistence restoration.
- Do not add modules, hierarchy, stateful or temporal nodes, pulse execution, or unsupported node families to the restricted projections.
- Do not fingerprint unchecked or blocking-invalid authored definitions as validated semantic networks.
- Do not derive identity from Rust type identity, debug formatting, discriminants, allocation order, hash iteration, diagnostic metadata, topological order, reaction-operation identity, SCC data, caches, or private representation.
- Do not introduce a late validation or compilation identity context or a new public bound-network lifecycle stage.
- Do not include `TopologyPatchSemanticsVersion` in the restricted network projection.

## Implementation obligations

- Respect every represented requirement of the three identity contracts after independent review.
- Preserve exact 16-byte `TimeDomainId` and distinct non-interchangeable 32-byte fingerprint value types.
- Require caller-owned time-domain identity before validation; `validate()` remains context-free and successful validation fixes one intrinsic semantic identity.
- Use domain version 1, `CoreSemanticsVersion(1)`, and `BuiltInNodeSemanticsVersion(1)`.
- Encode the exact canonical record field names, nesting, closed variant names, stable-key bytes, collection orders, and digest wrappers specified for both restricted projections.
- Use `mossignal/network_fingerprint/v1` and `mossignal/input_schema_fingerprint/v1` with unkeyed BLAKE3-256.
- Keep `InputSchemaFingerprint` independent of network identity and unrelated topology while network-bound artifacts later carry both identities separately.
- Ensure no public construction path can expose validated fingerprints for a blocking-invalid network.
- Leave item 13 able to carry both fingerprints and `TimeDomainId` unchanged without recomputation from dense layout.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Exact `NetworkBuilder` and `UncheckedNetwork` constructor spelling and argument grouping remain free so long as identity is caller-supplied before validation.
- Private projection structs, encoder decomposition, caching, helper names, and module layout are free when the authoritative canonical bytes remain exact.
- The narrow canonical encoder may be private and need not anticipate complete persistence encoding or decoding.

## Expected change surface

- a focused identity or fingerprint module under `crates/mossignal/src/`
- `crates/mossignal/src/authored.rs` for authored `TimeDomainId` ownership and access
- `crates/mossignal/src/validation.rs` for fingerprint construction only after successful validation
- `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs` for deliberate public identity exports
- `crates/mossignal/Cargo.toml` and the workspace lockfile for BLAKE3 and any minimal canonical-encoding support
- focused unit tests and versioned golden vectors
- the three identity contracts only for implementation-discovered reusable facts; any implementation-time change remains draft
- `.beads/` when implementation acceptance closes the bead

## Required verification

1. Equal stable semantic networks with permuted node, port, connection, and external-endpoint insertion order produce identical canonical bytes and fingerprints.
2. Metadata-only changes leave both fingerprints unchanged.
3. Changing only `TimeDomainId` changes `NetworkFingerprint`.
4. Changing only `NetworkKey` changes `NetworkFingerprint`.
5. Changing a Constant value changes `NetworkFingerprint`.
6. Changing connection incidence changes `NetworkFingerprint`.
7. Changing topological or private representation leaves both fingerprints unchanged.
8. Other topology changes that preserve the complete external-input schema preserve `InputSchemaFingerprint`.
9. Adding or removing an external input changes `InputSchemaFingerprint`.
10. Equal canonical payload bytes under the network and input-schema domains produce different digests.
11. Hand-reviewed golden canonical input bytes and expected BLAKE3-256 results cover a minimal network and a nontrivial Constant/Not network.
12. Blocking-invalid definitions cannot publish validated fingerprints.
13. `make check-dev`, then `make check-final` at implementation acceptance.

## Dependencies

- Roadmap item 11 / `ms-f2d` is complete and accepted.
- Roadmap item 13 depends on this bead producing intrinsic validated semantic identity for `CompiledNetwork`.
- Roadmap items 15 and 19 depend on the input-schema identity established here.

## Readiness

Reviewed and ready for implementation. The item-12 planning decisions are represented in authoritative specifications and reviewed contracts; no unresolved observable product question or later-roadmap dependency blocks this bounded slice.
close_reason: Implemented restricted semantic fingerprints and input-schema identity

title: Repair provenance-view identity isolation
description:
## Objective

Repair the result-owned provenance boundary so a CauseRef from one ProvenanceView cannot resolve through a different non-equivalent view, even when both views have the same topology, fingerprint, revision, transaction time, and current external level and pulse inputs.

This is architectural audit item 2 and a correctness bug, not a persistence redesign. At baseline 51a5063b2b653a6b5e1317c2a23685a8cb0bf0e2, CauseRef stores a scope token plus an ordinal, and the scope token is derived only from transaction coordinates and current external observations. Different prior machine histories can therefore produce different record graphs under the same token, allowing a valid ordinal from one view to resolve to an unrelated record in another.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed contracts used unchanged

- mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction
  - docs/specs/contracts/ready-level-transaction.yaml
  - rule: resolvable-ready-causes
  - role: every returned cause resolves through its successful owned immutable result view; later machine changes cannot invalidate it; private arena positions are not durable identity.
- mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction
  - docs/specs/contracts/initialization-transaction.yaml
  - role: initialization results own resolvable causes and publish provenance atomically.
- mossignal.runtime.temporal_event_execution
  - docs/specs/contracts/temporal-event-execution.yaml
  - role: due-event and pending-event causes remain stable, chronological, and failure-atomic across temporal transactions.
- mossignal.node.pulse_delay
  - docs/specs/contracts/pulse-delay.yaml
  - role: scheduled and emitted delayed pulses carry resolvable provenance across reactions.
- mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model
  - docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-problem-model.yaml
  - role: foreign and invalid cause conditions ultimately retain catalogue distinctions and typed evidence.
- mossignal.diagnostics.artifact_reports
  - docs/specs/contracts/artifact-reports.yaml
  - role: one atomic lookup failure remains a Result failure backed by the common problem model.

No contract changes are required. Full content-addressed persisted provenance, checkpointing, and retention policy are known future facets and are deliberately excluded.

## Included scope

- Add the failing regression first and observe the current foreign-view lookup succeed or otherwise demonstrate the scope collision before changing production code.
- Construct two independent machine histories that have:
  - the same compiled topology and network fingerprint;
  - the same topology revision;
  - the same requested transaction time;
  - the same current external level valuation and pulse batch;
  - different prior committed state, pending-event history, retained causal roots, or record graph content.
- Obtain valid causes at in-range ordinals from both successful result views.
- Prove each native cause resolves through its own view.
- Prove a cause from either view is rejected by the other view, including when the ordinal exists in both record vectors.
- Replace the transaction-coordinate-only scope with identity tied to the actual immutable provenance graph or its authoritative root set. A deterministic scope-neutral content hash, immutable content-addressed identity, or another collision-resistant view-owned design is acceptable.
- Remap all records, supporter references, output-event causes, state causes, pending-event causes, and machine-retained roots coherently when a view is finalized.
- Preserve cloning semantics: clones or shared handles to the same immutable view must continue to resolve its causes.
- Preserve out-of-range or malformed-cause rejection within the owning view.
- Preserve initialization, ready, pulse, stateful, and temporal provenance acyclicity and result ownership.

## Implementation obligations

- A scope computed only from NetworkKey, NetworkFingerprint, NetworkRevision, current time, and current external inputs is forbidden.
- Non-equivalent record graphs must not share a lookup authority merely because transaction coordinates match.
- Private ordinals may remain local storage positions, but they must be usable only with the owning graph/view identity.
- Do not use memory addresses, process randomness, timestamps, global mutable counters, or insertion-order accidents as semantic identity.
- Keep cause identity opaque and non-durable; do not expose the private ordinal or scope.
- Preserve deterministic equivalent execution behavior up to non-semantic cause-reference renaming.
- Preserve complete transaction failure atomicity and all existing budget accounting.
- Keep production code free of unwrap and expect.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No full Merkle DAG, persisted CauseDigest API, canonical snapshot provenance encoding, restoration, replay, or compatibility reader.
- No checkpoint-root design, provenance compaction, optional-history retention policy, or quadratic-history performance rewrite.
- No new explanation query family or why-not reasoning.
- No catalogue-wide operation-failure unification; the separate audit-item-5 bead owns systematic DiagnosticCode/ProblemEvidence projection. This bead must retain enough distinction for a foreign-view failure to be mapped correctly later.
- No public CauseRef field exposure or compatibility shim for the flawed private token.
- No unrelated transaction or event behavior change.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Choose the simplest deterministic identity construction that binds a CauseRef to the actual immutable graph/view and is practical before persisted content-addressed provenance exists.
- The private scope width, finalization pass, remapping helpers, and record storage organization may change.
- Equivalent independently built views may share a content identity if and only if every valid ordinal resolves to equivalent canonical record content and supporter structure.
- The exact private failure enum may remain narrow in this bead if foreign-view lookup is reliably rejected and later catalogue projection is not obstructed.

## Expected change surface

- crates/mossignal/src/transaction.rs for CauseRef, ProvenanceView, scope finalization, remapping, and lookup.
- Focused transaction/provenance regressions, with temporal or stateful fixtures as needed to create divergent histories.
- Possible narrow machine provenance-root plumbing changes if required to keep published causes coherent.
- No specification, contract, roadmap, persistence, or public explanation-system expansion.

## Required verification

1. The regression must fail before the fix and pass afterward.
2. Two histories with identical topology, revision, target time, and current external input but different provenance content must produce mutually isolated views.
3. A foreign cause whose ordinal is valid in the target view must still be rejected.
4. Native causes, every supporter reference, output-event causes, pending-event causes, state causes, and earlier retained result causes must remain resolvable through their owning view.
5. Clone/share behavior must preserve lookup authority for the same immutable view.
6. Malformed or out-of-range causes must remain rejected without panic.
7. Provenance must remain acyclic and terminate in authoritative roots across level, pulse, edge, toggle, and PulseDelay paths.
8. Equivalent execution remains deterministic up to private cause-reference renaming.
9. All relevant budget and failure-atomicity tests remain green.
10. Run the focused regression while iterating, then make check-dev; final acceptance additionally runs make check-final.

## Blocking questions

None. The ownership guarantee is specified. The exact private identity strategy is implementation freedom and does not require the future persistence model.

## Readiness

Open, bounded, and claimable.
acceptance_criteria: Completion requires a regression first demonstrating two distinct histories with identical topology, revision, transaction time, and current external inputs; view identity bound to actual provenance content or ownership; mutual rejection of foreign causes even at valid ordinals; native, cloned, temporal, and retained-result cause resolution preserved; no persistence/checkpoint scope expansion; focused tests passing; make check-dev passing; and make check-final passing at acceptance.
notes:
Implemented deterministic provenance-view identity from the finalized immutable record graph instead of transaction coordinates. CauseRef and ProvenanceView now use a private full-width BLAKE3 scope derived from network identity and a canonical scope-neutral encoding of every provenance record, including ordered record position, semantic subjects, logical times, revisions, external observations, pending PulseDelay facts, pulse contributions, results, and supporter ordinals. Each reaction builds under an unpublished placeholder scope, appends any scheduled pending-event records, computes the final graph identity, and coherently remaps record supporters, pulse contributions, operation causes, input/output roots, state roots, schedule roots, pending-event causes, and already-collected chronological output-event causes before publication.

Added the regression first and observed it fail at the foreign-view assertion: two machines with the same topology, revision, target time, current external level, empty pulse input, record count, and output-cause ordinal—but different prior transaction times—incorrectly resolved each other's causes. The regression now proves mutual foreign rejection, native cause and supporter resolution, clone authority preservation, and out-of-range rejection. Equivalent graph construction remains deterministic; no memory address, randomness, wall-clock time, global counter, or durable public cause representation was introduced.

No specification, contract, roadmap, persistence, checkpoint, or explanation-query changes.

Verification:
- failing regression observed before production fix
- cargo test -p mossignal provenance_views_reject_causes_from_different_converged_histories --lib
- cargo test -p mossignal --lib
- cargo test -p mossignal --test edge_detectors --test level_controlled_pulse --test module_execution --test pulse_foundation --test temporal_foundation
- cargo test -p mossignal --test pulse_combinational --test level_conveniences --test application_bindings
- cargo fmt --all
- git diff --check
- make check-dev
- make check-final
close_reason: Bound provenance lookup authority to finalized immutable graph content; cross-history causes are isolated and all focused and repository acceptance checks pass.

title: Add application bindings and bound execution façade
description:
## Objective

Implement Premium Continuation Roadmap item 40 as the first complete application-binding adapter: map caller-owned input and output identifiers to one compiled network's typed stable endpoints, project caller observations into ordinary snapshots and deltas, project outputs back to caller identifiers, and provide a thin bound-machine façade without changing machine semantics.

## Roadmap provenance

- Document: `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md`
- Item: 40
- Title: Application bindings and bound execution façade

This provenance records sequencing only. The referenced contracts and authoritative specifications govern product semantics.

## Contract basis

### Reviewed feature contract

- `mossignal.binding.application_adapter`
  - `docs/specs/contracts/application-bindings.yaml`
  - status: reviewed
  - role: governs caller-owned non-semantic identifiers, compiled-schema binding, bidirectional mapping, input and output projection, binding failures, and bound-machine equivalence.

### Reviewed contracts reused without modification

- `mossignal.compile.compiled_network` (`docs/specs/contracts/compiled-network.yaml`): immutable compiled topology, retained stable network/input-schema identity, graph access, and machine/input-builder entry points. Only unchanged identity, topology, and opaque-dense facets are reused; changed validation-owner source facets are outside this task.
- `mossignal.runtime.level_input_snapshot` (`docs/specs/contracts/level-input-snapshot.yaml`) and `mossignal.runtime.level_input_delta` (`docs/specs/contracts/level-input-delta.yaml`): exact-bound owned input artifacts, complete level snapshots, delta omission/retention, typed observations, and structured input failures. Only unchanged represented facets apply; prepared-patch targets remain outside this task.
- `mossignal.runtime.reaction_scoped_pulse_foundation` (`docs/specs/contracts/reaction-scoped-pulse-foundation.yaml`): typed pulse observations, checked multiplicity, reaction-scoped publication, and absence of persistent current pulse values. Only unchanged non-fingerprint facets apply.
- `mossignal.runtime.machine_lifecycle` (`docs/specs/contracts/machine-lifecycle.yaml`), `mossignal.runtime.initialization_transaction` (`docs/specs/contracts/initialization-transaction.yaml`), and `mossignal.runtime.ready_level_transaction` (`docs/specs/contracts/ready-level-transaction.yaml`): canonical machine ownership, lifecycle, transaction, scheduling, provenance, result, and failure-atomicity semantics that the façade must preserve.
- `mossignal.diagnostics.problem_model` (`docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-problem-model.yaml`) and `mossignal.diagnostics.subject_references` (`docs/specs/contracts/diagnostic-subject-references.yaml`): catalogue-backed failure conditions, typed evidence, and binding-slot subject identity. The changed authoritative binding-subject section was rechecked during preparation; canonical ordering for later SubjectRef variants remains known-uncovered and is not required by this leaf-failure slice.

## Included scope

- Add a public binding module containing immutable `BindingSet<I, O>`, its compiled-network-borrowing builder, `InputProjector<D, I>`, projected output values, and a minimal `BoundMachine<D, I, O>` façade.
- Bind caller-owned input and output identifiers to typed external endpoints from exactly one `CompiledNetwork<D>` while retaining network, topology-revision, and input-schema compatibility context.
- Provide deterministic endpoint-to-caller and caller-to-endpoint lookup for Level and Pulse inputs and outputs without exposing private compiled positions.
- Reject unknown endpoints, wrong-kind paths, duplicate endpoints, duplicate or ambiguous caller identifiers, incomplete requested projections, wrong networks, and stale topology revisions or schemas through structured binding failures and the applicable catalogue codes/evidence.
- Project caller-keyed Level and Pulse observations into ordinary `InputSnapshot<D>` and `InputDelta<D>` values by delegating through the compiled network's existing builders.
- Project every ordinary LevelEstablished, LevelChanged, and Pulsed output event to its caller output identifier while retaining exact values/counts, time, cause, revision, and order.
- Expose ready current Level output observation by caller identifier through the existing machine baseline; do not invent current Pulse state.
- Provide a small bound-machine façade that owns or wraps one compatible ordinary machine and binding set, supports initialization and ready advancement from caller observations, and returns projected outputs alongside access to the unchanged ordinary result/provenance.
- Add focused public-surface, exact-projection, diagnostics, determinism, and direct-versus-bound execution equivalence tests.

## Exclusions and non-goals

- No callbacks, observer subscriptions, delivery cursors, acknowledgement state, async runtime integration, or event-handler registry.
- No domain-specific entity model, payload transport, arbitrary signal values, or caller object-model interpretation.
- No replacement or deprecation of structural endpoint-key APIs, ordinary input builders, transactions, or `Machine<D>`.
- No module-instance binding changes, authored graph semantics, new evaluator path, new node kind, runtime policy change, or provenance rewriting.
- No persistence or codecs for caller identifiers/binding sets, binding participation in snapshots or replay frames, or fingerprint/schema changes.
- No topology patch implementation, automatic rebinding, migration, stale-projector refresh, or compatibility shim for earlier repository revisions.
- No general bound inspection/explanation/state-change façade beyond current external Level outputs and projected output events.

## Implementation obligations

- Implement the `mossignal.binding.application_adapter` requirements `caller-owned-nonsemantic-identifiers`, `immutable-compiled-schema-adapter`, `unambiguous-bidirectional-mapping`, `binding-construction-failures`, `exact-input-projection`, `lossless-output-projection`, `bindings-outside-machine-semantics`, and `bound-machine-is-equivalent-delegation`.
- Build endpoint inventories from stable public graph/schema information or the smallest new read-only compiled accessor; never expose or bind through dense execution indices.
- Preserve signal kind in every mapping. Caller identifiers remain opaque equality/hash keys and never determine semantics, ordering, fingerprints, diagnostics identity, or evaluator behavior.
- Make safe completed mapping/projection state immutable. Validate all inputs needed by a multi-binding or projection operation before publishing a completed artifact; failed operations must not partially mutate an existing immutable artifact or machine.
- Reuse `CompiledNetwork::input_snapshot` and `CompiledNetwork::input_delta` as the canonical artifact builders so projected artifacts retain exact network and input-schema identity and all existing Level/Pulse boundary laws.
- Keep output projection lossless except for substituting the uniquely bound caller output identifier. Preserve the ordinary `TransactionResult` and its `ProvenanceView`; do not copy, normalize, or fabricate causes.
- Ensure `BoundMachine` delegates to `Machine::apply`, preserves the ordinary result and failure, and exposes access to the underlying semantic machine/bindings sufficient to demonstrate that scheduling, policy, lifecycle, revision, digests where implemented, and failure atomicity are unchanged.
- Integrate binding conditions into the existing structured failure/diagnostic model without requiring caller identifiers to become `SubjectRef` identity or rendered strings.
- Keep production code free of `unwrap` and `expect`.

## Allowed implementation freedom

- Choose the smallest deterministic map/set representation and iteration order. Record and test the concrete order without making caller identifier ordering semantic or requiring `Ord`.
- Choose whether `BindingSetBuilder::finish` requires all bindings or permits a partial immutable set whose requested projector/façade rejects missing mappings; every successful requested projection must be complete and unambiguous.
- Choose concise owned caller-observation builder types or direct methods for snapshot/delta projection. The exact method grouping, borrowing, iterator types, and projected output wrapper names are free if the typed responsibilities and failure distinctions remain clear.
- Choose whether the minimal `BoundMachine` owns or is constructed from an ordinary machine, and whether projection helpers return paired ordinary/projected results or a wrapper with accessors. Favor the simplest design that preserves direct access to canonical semantic artifacts and proves equivalence.
- Where safe typed APIs make an ambiguity unrepresentable, retain the catalogue condition in the failure/code mapping and test the preventing invariant rather than adding a malformed public constructor solely to emit it.

## Expected change surface

- A focused public binding module under `crates/mossignal/src/`, plus deliberate exports from `crates/mossignal/src/lib.rs`.
- Narrow read-only external-endpoint/schema access in `crates/mossignal/src/validation.rs`, `crates/mossignal/src/compile.rs`, or an existing graph view if required.
- `crates/mossignal/src/diagnostics.rs` only for the applicable binding codes, evidence, subjects, and leaf failure integration not already present.
- Focused integration tests such as `crates/mossignal/tests/application_bindings.rs` and only narrowly required shared test support.
- `docs/premium_continuation_roadmap.md` for the item-40 progress/completion heading.
- `.beads` only when implementation is later closed and synchronized.

## Required verification

1. Bind mixed Level/Pulse inputs and outputs in permuted insertion orders and prove the same immutable bidirectional endpoint mappings without requiring caller-key ordering.
2. Exercise unknown endpoint, wrong signal kind where dynamically reachable, duplicate endpoint, duplicate caller identifier, missing required mapping, wrong network, and stale topology revision or schema failures; structurally verify applicable codes, subjects, evidence, and absence of ambiguous suggestions.
3. Build complete snapshots and partial deltas from caller identifiers, including Level completeness/retention, absent and nonzero Pulse observations, duplicate/conflicting/unknown caller observations, and exact underlying network/input-schema identities.
4. Compare projector-produced snapshots/deltas with direct structural-key artifacts for the same observations and verify identical ordinary transaction behavior.
5. Project LevelEstablished, LevelChanged, and Pulsed events and assert exact caller output, value/count, time, cause, revision, and flat ordering while the retained cause resolves through the unchanged ordinary provenance view.
6. Verify ready current Level output lookup in both endpoint and caller directions, structured absence before initialization or for unknown/unbound keys, and no persistent current Pulse observation.
7. Run equivalent initialization and later transactions through direct `Machine` and `BoundMachine` paths and compare lifecycle, time, revision, output stream, settled outputs, schedule, provenance, runtime policy, and available state/observable digests after only caller-key normalization.
8. Inject projection, compatibility, runtime, and budget failures and prove both direct and bound paths return equivalent structured failures and preserve the complete machine unchanged.
9. Prove bindings do not change authored/compiled structure, NetworkFingerprint, InputSchemaFingerprint, machine/replay identity, scheduling, evaluator operation, provenance subjects, or diagnostics unrelated to binding validation.
10. Run focused Rust tests while iterating, then `make check-dev`; final acceptance additionally runs `make check-final`.

## Blocking questions

None. The specifications fix the adapter boundary, identity separation, failure conditions, and semantic-equivalence requirement. Storage, completeness timing, caller-observation API shape, projected wrapper shape, and bound-machine ownership are bounded implementation freedoms with deterministic testable choices.

## Readiness

Ready as a bounded implementation task. The `mossignal.binding.application_adapter` contract is independently reviewed, and no product-semantics blocker remains.
